canonical_seed.student_text:
A train moves in a straight line at a steady 18 m/s while its forces balance. Which condition describes it?
A. static equilibrium
B. dynamic equilibrium
C. unbalanced motion
D. no-force motion

canonical_seed.solution_text: Balanced forces with nonzero constant velocity are dynamic equilibrium.

canonical_seed.student_text:
A book lies motionless on a shelf. Which statement is correct?
A. No forces act because the book is at rest.
B. Only gravity acts.
C. Gravity downward and shelf support upward act and balance.
D. A force of rest points upward.
canonical_seed.student_html:
A book lies motionless on a shelf. Which statement is correct?

  1. No forces act because the book is at rest.
  2. Only gravity acts.
  3. Gravity downward and shelf support upward act and balance.
  4. A force of rest points upward.
choices: No forces act because the book is at rest.
Gravity downward and shelf support upward act and balance.
A force of rest points upward.
canonical_seed.answer: C — Gravity downward and shelf support upward act and balance.
canonical_seed.solution_text: Rest does not mean no forces; the support and weight forces can be equal and opposite.
canonical_seed.solution_html: Rest does not mean no forces; the support and weight forces can be equal and opposite.

canonical_seed.student_text:
A drone flies straight east at constant speed while maintaining constant altitude. Which statement best explains why it can be in equilibrium?
A. Equilibrium requires the drone to be at rest.
B. Its velocity can be constant while the net force is zero.
C. A moving object must have a net force east.
D. Its weight disappears while flying.
canonical_seed.student_html:
A drone flies straight east at constant speed while maintaining constant altitude. Which statement best explains why it can be in equilibrium?

  1. Equilibrium requires the drone to be at rest.
  2. Its velocity can be constant while the net force is zero.
  3. A moving object must have a net force east.
  4. Its weight disappears while flying.
choices: Equilibrium requires the drone to be at rest.
Its velocity can be constant while the net force is zero.
A moving object must have a net force east.
canonical_seed.answer: B — Its velocity can be constant while the net force is zero.
canonical_seed.solution_text: Dynamic equilibrium is constant velocity with zero net force.
canonical_seed.solution_html: Dynamic equilibrium is constant velocity with zero net force.

canonical_seed.student_text:
A warehouse robot moves straight right at constant speed. Its force model is shown. Is the model consistent with that motion? Explain using both axes.

          120 N up
             ↑
65 N left ← [robot] → 65 N right
             ↓
          120 N down
canonical_seed.student_html:
A warehouse robot moves straight right at constant speed. Its force model is shown. Is the model consistent with that motion? Explain using both axes.

          120 N up
             ↑
65 N left ← [robot] → 65 N right
             ↓
          120 N down
canonical_seed.answer: Yes. Left/right forces cancel and up/down forces cancel, so the total net force is zero and constant velocity is possible.
canonical_seed.solution_text: Yes. Left/right forces cancel and up/down forces cancel, so the total net force is zero and constant velocity is possible.
canonical_seed.solution_html: Yes. Left/right forces cancel and up/down forces cancel, so the total net force is zero and constant velocity is possible.

canonical_seed.student_text:
A cart is moving right at constant speed with 32 N pull right and 32 N resistance left. The resistance suddenly drops to 20 N while the pull stays 32 N. What happens?
A. It keeps exactly the same velocity.
B. It accelerates to the right.
C. It accelerates to the left.
D. It stops because forces are no longer equal.
canonical_seed.student_html:
A cart is moving right at constant speed with 32 N pull right and 32 N resistance left. The resistance suddenly drops to 20 N while the pull stays 32 N. What happens?

  1. It keeps exactly the same velocity.
  2. It accelerates to the right.
  3. It accelerates to the left.
  4. It stops because forces are no longer equal.
choices: It keeps exactly the same velocity.
It stops because forces are no longer equal.
canonical_seed.answer: B — It accelerates to the right.
canonical_seed.solution_text: The new net force is 12 N right, so velocity changes toward the right.
canonical_seed.solution_html: The new net force is 12 N right, so velocity changes toward the right.
